techniques.name: Travis Picking Masterclass
techniques.description: A steady alternating bass line on strings 5 and 4 played by the thumb, while index and middle fingers syncopate on strings 2 and 3 with rapid hammer-ons and pull-offs

sequence: Establish strict alternating thumb pattern between string 5 and string 4
Pinch string 5 and string 2 simultaneously on beat 1
Pluck string 3 with index finger on the upbeat, thumb on string 4 on beat 2
Execute smooth 2nd-string finger lifts for Cmaj7 and pinky additions for Cadd9
tips: Practice the thumb bass pattern in isolation until it is completely automated
Keep the hand anchored lightly with the forearm against the lower guitar bout
Ensure every note in the alternating Travis pattern sounds evenly balanced in volume

beginner.title: Isolate the Alternating Thumb
steps: Hold a standard C chord shape
Practice picking only strings 5 and 4 with the thumb at 60 BPM
Ensure steady quarter-note time without wavering
Gradually introduce the index finger on string 3

intermediate.title: Integrate the 2nd-String Suspensions
steps: Add the middle finger picking string 2 on the downbeat
Practice the C → Cmaj7 → Cadd9 finger movement
Apply the exact same picking pattern to the Am chord shape
Smooth the transition between C and Am at 80 BPM

advanced.title: Master Studio Nuance & Full Performance
steps: Bring the entire intro up to album tempo of 94 BPM
Perform the full verse and chorus transitions seamlessly
Achieve perfect dynamic balance between alternating bass and upper melody

commonMistakes: Letting the alternating thumb drift off-tempo when fingers change shapes
Hitting the 1st string accidentally instead of isolating string 2
Rushing the tempo beyond 94 BPM, losing the reflective philosophical sway
practiceRoutine: 3 minutes: Thumb-only alternating bass drill on strings 5 and 4
5 minutes: Isolated 2nd-string melody movement (C - Cmaj7 - Cadd9)
5 minutes: Full intro pattern with metronome at 80 BPM
5 minutes: Verse G/B bass walkdown transition
focusAreas: Dynamic separation between bass and melody
metronomeWork: Start at 70 BPM with clicks on eighth notes
Advance to 94 BPM with quarter-note clicks once thumb independence is achieved
Verify your right hand doesn't rush during the Am suspension measure
